newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrea ready to send force to central Africa.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea ready to send force to central Africa.

text.p: Eritrea is ready to send troops to join a multinational intervention force in eastern Zaire, Foreign Minister Petros Solomon told Reuters on Wednesday.

"The President has confirmed to the Secretary General of the OAU (Organisation of African Unity), Mr Salim Ahmed Salim, that Eritrea will contribute to an international intervention force," Petros told Reuters.
"The force is ready to leave at any time," he said. He said Eritrea was ready to send up to one brigade.
President Isaias Afewerki attended a regional crisis summit nine days ago in Kenya where African leaders asked the United Nations to send a force to help 1.2 million refugees in eastern Zaire.
Canada has agreed to lead the force and other countries that have offered to take part include Spain, France, Mali, Ethiopia, Italy and South Africa.
Eritrea, Africa's youngest nation, fought a 30 year liberation war against Ethiopia 1961-1991. It became formally independent following a referendum in 1993.
